entries.text: kitfunso hippo-memory hippo service a local-first, sqlite-backed memory system for ai agents that stores project and global memories, retrieves context through a cli, mcp, http, and integrations, and applies decay, retrieval strengthening, and sleep consolidation to its memory layers. teams or individuals wanting persistent context across cli agent tools and projects agent workflows that need inspectable local memory, recall, and session handoffs ai-and-automation agent-memory ai-agents cli mcp local-first self-hosted multi-agent web-ui open-source build-ai-products improve-developer-workflow typescript nodejs sqlite buffer, episodic, and semantic memory layers with consolidation and decay cli commands for initialization, recall, capture, import, snapshots, and handoffs stdio mcp server plus http api and an openclaw plugin optional hybrid retrieval that combines bm25 with local or configured embeddings markdown mirrors alongside the sqlite store for inspection and git tracking cross-tool imports from chatgpt exports, claude files, cursor rules, markdown, and text cli mcp server http api local web dashboard openclaw plugin npm global package python sdk source build typescript javascript python sqlite node.js model context protocol vitest mit mit license offers one local memory layer across several agent clients and projects makes recall explainable and persists both long-term and active-task context supports a no-embedding bm25 fallback while allowing optional hybrid retrieval requires node.js 22.5 or later for the primary npm package hippo init can create project stores, patch agent instruction files, alter a detected codex launcher, and install a daily runner unless disabled embedding-backed retrieval is optional; entries.text: rtk-ai rtk rtk cli a rust command-line proxy for coding-agent workflows that runs supported developer commands, filters their output before it reaches the llm context, tracks resulting token savings, and can install agent-specific hooks or instruction-based integrations. coding-agent users who want more compact shell-command context without changing their normal developer commands teams that want local token-savings analytics and configurable command-output filtering developer-tools coding-agents cli context-engineering token-usage developer-productivity git testing improve-developer-workflow rust filters, groups, truncates, and deduplicates output from more than 100 supported developer commands provides compact wrappers for files, git and github cli, tests, builds, linters, containers, cloud, and data commands installs hooks, plugins, or rules for supported coding assistants to rewrite eligible shell commands automatically stores token-savings history and exposes gain, session, and discovery analytics commands saves full command output on configured failures so an agent can inspect it without rerunning the command offers per-user and per-project configuration for filters, excluded commands, tracking, output, and telemetry cli coding-agent hooks coding-agent plugins agent instruction and rule files local analytics commands homebrew linux or macos install script pre-built binaries cargo source installation rust sqlite cargo homebrew coding-agent hooks ripgrep integration apache-2.0 apache license 2.0 reduces command-output noise at the command boundary while preserving an explicit path to full failure output covers a broad set of everyday development commands and several coding-assistant integration styles provides local tracking and configuration rather than requiring a hosted optimization service the retained release feed is dominated by newer 0.44.0 development release candidates; the package manifest and changelog identify v0.42.4 as the latest stable release automatic rewriting applies only to the integration tier supported by each agent; instruction-file integrations such as codex depend on the model following the generated instructions hooks operate on shell commands, so built-in assistant tools such as claude code read, grep, and glob bypass the automatic rewrite path another unrelated project uses the rtk crate name; entries.text: zakirullin cognitive-load cognitive load is what matters documentation a living software-design guide that argues for reducing extraneous cognitive load through concrete examples of code structure, abstraction, dependencies, services, and interfaces. developers and teams reviewing design choices for maintainability readers looking for practical examples of simpler, easier-to-change code documentation-and-learning documentation reference developer-productivity improve-developer-workflow learn-and-reference distinguishes intrinsic task difficulty from reducible extraneous cognitive load uses examples of complex conditionals, nesting, and inheritance to discuss simpler control flow and composition explains deep versus shallow modules and the cost of excessive indirection examines microservices, framework coupling, layered architecture, and premature abstraction recommends self-describing interfaces and carefully scoped dependencies links to supporting reading and provides translated versions of the guide markdown guide web documentation read the repository readme clone repository cc-by-4.0 creative commons attribution 4.0 international focuses on a memorable decision criterion rather than a single prescribed architecture concrete code and system-design examples make the principles quick to apply in reviews covers both local code structure and broader service and dependency boundaries the guide is explicitly opinionated and should be balanced against a project's domain and operational constraints it is a reading resource, not a tool that measures or enforces cognitive load some examples and linked supporting material reflect the author's interpretation rather than a formal standard 🧠 cognitive load is what matters
